notes: Golden set for the classifier. Sensitive cases MUST produce the listed sensitive category (zero false negatives allowed; the test fails if any sensitive case is missed). Serve cases must produce no sensitive flags and a commercial_intent within [intent_min, intent_max]. categories_any means at least one listed category must appear. The band on a sensitive case states what the merge guarantees rather than a judgement about the text: a non-empty sensitive list caps commercial_intent at 0.2 (RULES_DATA.scoring.sensitive.max_intent) and self_harm forces 0, so s007 and s010 are deliberately high-intent texts that must still come back capped. A case may also carry `messages`, the conversation it arrived in, oldest first: `text` is then the content of its LAST user turn and the classifier is driven with the whole array, because prepareText keeps the last 4 user and assistant turns. Those cases exist because a single sentence cannot express the shapes that matter - a product question after a debugging exchange (high intent that reads as coding help), or a shopping question whose sensitive context was established two turns earlier - and a prompt regression that only shows up in conversation is invisible to a golden set of terse sentences (progress.txt, CLASSIFIER-EVAL). Add cases here whenever a real conversation exposes a gap; never delete a sensitive case. `pnpm --filter @adgateio/gateway eval-classifier` scores a real model against this file.
